sections.h2: Offices that handle McAllen property tax
sections.html:
McAllen is in Hidalgo County, and a McAllen bill usually stacks the city, the county, a school district such as McAllen ISD and South Texas College, with special districts on some parcels. The Hidalgo County Appraisal District sets values. The City of McAllen Tax Office sends the city's own statement. For ownership or mailing address changes, visit the appraisal district at 4405 Professional Drive, Edinburg, TX 78539, telephone (956) 381-8466.

The county's 2025 rate schedule prints these rates per $100 of value for the other units that tax McAllen property:

  • Hidalgo County: $0.57500
  • McAllen ISD: $0.93220
  • South Texas College: $0.16200

The city's own 2025 rate is $0.448989 per $100, as printed on its tax notice. Add them together for a full-rate picture, then subtract any exemptions on your file. Mail for the city tax office goes to P.O. Box 220, McAllen, TX 78505-0220.

Texas gives McAllen owners until January 31 to pay. A deadline that falls on a weekend slides to the next business day, and statements usually go out in October. For the 2026 bill, the last penalty-free day is Monday, February 1, 2027.

Charges begin on February 1. Interest adds one percentage point each month until the account is paid, and the schedule continues past July, reaching a 24 percent total the following January.

Penalty and interest by month
MonthPenaltyInterestTotal
February6%1%7%
March7%2%9%
April8%3%11%
May9%4%13%
June10%5%15%
July12%6%18%

A separate 15 percent collection charge applies to accounts still open on July 1 (April 1 for personal property). A firm hired to collect can add up to 20 percent, so read any collection letter closely.

The city's 2026 hearing notice proposed $0.448989 per $100, the same as 2025. It printed a no-new-revenue rate of $0.444778 and a voter-approval rate of $0.517054, and it said the proposal is under the voter-approval ceiling, so no election is needed. For the final 2026 rate, call the tax office at (956) 681-1330.

The notice put the average homestead taxable value at $217,661 for 2025 and $221,213 for 2026, with the total levy on all properties falling 1.10 percent.

The city's slice is one piece of the total. The county, school district and college each set their own rates every fall, and taxing units have until about September 29, or 60 days after they receive the certified roll if that is later, to do so.

sections.h2: Exemptions that reduce a McAllen bill
sections.html:
The city offers $10,000 for each owner who has reached 65, $10,000 for a disabled person, and $5,000 to $12,000 for a disabled veteran depending on rating. A 100 percent disabled veteran's residence homestead is fully exempt. Applications and address corrections go to the chief appraiser at the Hidalgo County Appraisal District.

  • School homestead: $140,000 of value is removed for McAllen ISD taxes on a residence homestead.
  • Older or disabled owners: $60,000 more comes off school taxes, and the school tax bill on that home generally cannot climb after the owner qualifies.
  • Value cap: a homestead's appraised value may rise at most 10 percent per year, starting the January after the exemption begins.
  • Filing window: most exemption applications are due before May 1, though disabled veteran applicants may file later.

Someone who buys after January 1 can sometimes claim the exemption right away if the seller never received it.

Homeowners who are 65 or over, disabled, or disabled veteran owners with a homestead exemption can split the bill into four equal parts with no penalty or interest by asking no later than January 31. The parts fall due January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31. The same group may seek a tax deferral, and while one is in force the taxing unit cannot collect against or foreclose on the home the owner lives in.

  • Mail: send a check or money order to City of McAllen Tax Office, P.O. Box 220, with no convenience fee. Mail postmarked by the delinquency date counts as timely.
  • Online: a card payment carries a $3.00 fee when the total is $100.00 or less and a 3 percent fee on larger amounts. An eCheck carries a flat service fee from $3.00 on small bills up to $30.00 on bills of $15,000.01 or more.
  • Drop box: the tax office has payment flaps, one inside the lobby and one outside on the Cedar Avenue side. Put the payment and a copy of your statement in a sealed envelope, and leave cash out.
  • Email bills: owners who enroll in eNotification before October 17 get that year's bill by email.

When a mortgage company pays from escrow, the lender must tell the tax office which accounts it covers, and unpaid accounts get a courtesy reminder in mid-January. Never receiving the bill does not waive the penalty.

A protest must reach the Hidalgo County appraisal review board by May 15 or, if your notice arrives late, within 30 days of delivery. Homestead notices are mailed about April 1 and other property notices about May 1. Hearings begin around mid-May.

After the board rules, you can sue in district court, ask for binding arbitration or, for values above $1,000,000, take the case to SOAH, the State Office of Administrative Hearings. An appeal generally stays valid only if the undisputed portion of the tax is paid before it turns delinquent.

McAllen has 150,640 residents, up from 142,210 at the 2020 census. Owners occupy 59.5 percent of homes, and the middle owned-home value is $190,400. Mortgage holders report monthly costs near $1,764, renters pay about $1,049, and middle household income is $61,579.

sections.h2: Selling a McAllen house when you owe tax
sections.html:
Back taxes are normally cleared at closing, because delinquent tax stands in the way of clean title. A lien for each year's tax attaches on January 1, and whoever owns the house that day remains liable for that year's tax after a sale.

Texas offers relief before things reach that point. Penalty and interest can sometimes be waived: the request goes in writing before day 181 after delinquency, and the tax itself must be paid within 21 days of the owner learning of the debt. Some collectors allow plans stretching to 36 months, and a residence homestead must be offered one. For questions about delinquent notices, the collection law firm at Lone Star Plaza, 1512 S Lone Star Wy, Edinburg, (956) 383-4500, has a Hidalgo County office.

Behind on the bill and thinking of a fast as-is sale? Send the property address and the balance on your statement. Ask the tax office for an itemized payoff first, so you know what the title company will pay from your proceeds.

faqs.q: What is the McAllen property tax rate?
faqs.a: The City of McAllen's 2025 rate is $0.448989 per $100 of value, and the 2026 proposal repeats it. Hidalgo County, McAllen ISD and South Texas College add their own rates, which the county tax office publishes on its rate schedule.

faqs.q: When are McAllen property taxes due?
faqs.a: January 31 is the annual deadline, and a weekend date slides to the next business day. Penalties begin the day after the deadline.

faqs.q: Does McAllen offer a homeowner exemption?
faqs.a: The city offers $10,000 for owners 65 or older and $10,000 for disabled persons, plus disabled veteran exemptions, but no percentage homestead exemption. McAllen ISD applies the statewide $140,000 residence homestead exemption.

faqs.q: Can I pay McAllen property taxes in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, for homeowners past 65, disabled homeowners and disabled veteran owners who hold a residence homestead exemption and ask by January 31. Four equal payments fall due January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31.

faqs.q: Which phone number reaches the McAllen appraisal office?
faqs.a: Value questions go to the Hidalgo County Appraisal District at (956) 381-8466. The City of McAllen Tax Office handles billing at (956) 681-1330.
